Egyek Jewish Cemetery 1

Jewish Cemetery · Egyek, Hungary

Not demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries in Egyek, established after 1870, though its oldest tombstone (1871) was likely relocated here from the village's other, since-destroyed cemetery. Most local Jews worked in trade, crafts, farming, or as private officials; the community purchased cemetery land and founded its burial society in 1860, later building a synagogue in 1905 (since demolished). Population reached 142 by 1910, falling to 107 (of 7,473 residents) by 1941. During the 'White Terror' period, Jewish shops were smashed and the synagogue stoned; from 1938, authorities revoked industrial licenses, closing Jewish-owned businesses and even restricting what one shopkeeper could sell, before expropriating Jewish-owned land. By 1944, the Orthodox community had 86 members (20 taxpayers) led by president Arnold Domán, with only a caretaker rather than a rabbi.
